P1.evidence: P1a partial, and the best P1a in the batch — the rep had demonstrably read the application and used it: 'And I saw in the application that you run your own company, correct?' It scores partial rather than hit because it was one fact deployed mid-baseline as a question, not a read-back at the open designed to make the prospect feel seen. P1b partial: three of the four parts — 'I just want to understand. What's going on? What have you tried? And where are you trying to get to?' — with 'what you need' again absent. P1c hit: 'Sounds good?' asked and answered, 'Yeah, of course.' P1d hit: 'walk me through, like, what's been going on? Like, what's the main thing you're looking to fix right now?', and he re-asked it verbatim after the audio problems were resolved rather than letting it drop.

P2.evidence: Comfortably the strongest baseline in the batch and the only one with no outright misses. P2a hit — all three asked directly and in sequence: 'how old you right now?', 'roughly how tall are you?', 'what's your weight currently?' P2b hit, and the best execution of this check anywhere in the batch: he opened from the application, then tested the nature of the work ('Management work? Sitting in front of the desk?'), then quantified it rather than accepting a vague answer — 'if you would say, percentage-wise, 50% of the day you spent in front of the desk or more?' — which produced 70% seated. P2c partial: 'Any other chronic conditions and anything?' was asked, but hereditary history was never raised and the high blood pressure surfaced later, volunteered rather than elicited. P2d hit and thorough: 'Do you have like any injuries or anything that is limiting your movement right now?', then refusing the vague answer with 'What do you mean, not so good?', then establishing the ten-year duration, then probing a specific region on a hypothesis — 'How about the hips? Like do you feel...' — which uncovered the one-sided restriction. P2e partial: 'did you, like before that, did you do any workouts? Did you go to the gym?' produced the steroid history and the current two-week block, but he never established how many days a week the prospect actually trains now. P2f partial: never asked as a results question, though the most important result — new back pain from self-taught kettlebell work — was uncovered by 'Does it result, like, do you have back pains also?' P2g hit: 'in terms of nutrition, like how do you eat right now?', then 'any particular diet?', then the useful compliance probe 'what's your favorite food?' which produced 'if anything is sweet, it's my favorite food'. P2h partial: sleep was never asked directly and never probed for quality; it fell out of the working-hours question, and when the answer came back as roughly six hours the rep replied 'Okay. Not bad.' For a hypertensive 39-year-old who has just attributed his own fat gain to cortisol, six hours is a finding to work, not a pass. P2i hit: 'how do you feel, like, on a day-to-day, like, with energy and everything?' produced the crashes, the supplements and the stress.

P3.evidence: P3a hit: 'if you would have one goal that you would like to achieve right now, like, what would it be? Like, what's the focus right now?' P3b miss — the mobility/strength/energy menu was never offered. P3c hit, and the best-placed question on the call: 'Do you sometimes ran out of breath when she's running around?' produced the emotional centre of the whole conversation — 'sometimes they like to run out, but I cannot keep, I cannot, I think I'm too fat for that.' P3d, P3e, P3f and P3g all partial for the same recurring reason: the rep found the right territory and then supplied the meaning himself instead of asking for it. He asked 'do you have kids?' as a fact-finder and then delivered the significance as a monologue — 'guys who have kids... they tend to perform better. Because that's the biggest driver for them, that you want to be there healthy... you want to play with them.' Likewise on the goal he asserted the consequence and asked only for confirmation: 'imagine that you would actually lose this excessive weight, I don't know, 10, 15 kilos, that would probably allow you to do that, yeah?' The prospect had just handed him 'I'm too fat to keep up with my daughters' and the correct next move was silence and 'what does that feel like?', not a paragraph. Telling is that the prospect then redirected the conversation himself, to his blood pressure. P3h not_applicable — the reflect-back had not yet been reached when the recording stopped; the phase was still in progress.

P4.evidence: P4a hit — asked in the frame and then pursued directly with 'did you, like before that, did you do any workouts? Did you go to the gym?', which produced the year of steroid-assisted heavy training. P4b hit and asked cleanly: 'So, what happened? Like, why this excessive weight? What happened?' P4c partial — the cause was pursued, but the rep supplied the hypothesis rather than letting the prospect reach it: 'is it connected, like the stress levels that you have in your work, and you probably tend to eat more when you're stressed?' A leading question that happened to be right. P4d partial — the stress-eating loop was identified but never framed as the one thing in the way. P4e partial — the prospect did name his own gap, and named it well ('I'm struggling to not do that... one half of your body says, come, let's eat something more'), but he was walked there rather than getting there. P4f miss, and it is the most expensive omission in the recorded portion. The scripted line is 'the information isn't the problem — why can't you stick to it on your own?', and this prospect had spent two weeks proving the answer: he had Trevor's free videos, bought the kettlebells, started on his own, and given himself back pain. 'Maybe I do something wrong' was an open invitation and the rep acknowledged it warmly ('It's good to start, you know. That's the first step') instead of using it. The phase was still live when the recording cut, so this may have been run afterwards — but it was not run at the moment it was handed to him.

P5.evidence: The consequence frame was demonstrably being initiated at the exact moment the recording ends. P5a partial: 'Look, I'm going to be brutally honest with you. You're 39... We're not getting any younger, you're 105 kilos, the lifestyle that you're living right now, the amount of stress that you have, and the...' — the prospect answered 'Very heavy.' and the file stops mid-sentence. The move was started and its content is unobservable, so it is scored partial rather than credited or penalised. P5b, P5c and P5d are not_applicable because the recording, not the call, ended before them. Whoever re-pulls this file should re-score the phase: on the evidence of the opening line the rep was running Phase 5 properly and in the right order, before any presentation, which is more than can be said for the other closer calls in this batch.

P6.evidence: Not reached in the recorded portion — the transcript ends inside Phase 5. Scored N/A because the artifact is truncated, not because the rep skipped it; no inference either way is available.

P11.evidence: No offer, no price and no close attempt appear anywhere in the recorded portion, so the payment and onboarding sequence was never reachable within the artifact.

objection_plays.detail: A self-reliance objection with no scripted play: 'the change, it will not come, definitely not come from you. It will come from me. You can say whatever you want if I don't do it.' None of the five plays map — it is not money, timing, a spouse, a delay or fear; it is a prospect pre-emptively discounting the value of any coach. The rep handled it about as well as improvisation allows, conceding the true part and converting it into the accountability argument: 'Trevor is the best in this space when it comes to kettlebells, but it's going to be you that's going to be doing the work. He can coach you, he can keep you accountable, but you have to show up every day.' Scored partial rather than hit because the prospect did not visibly move on — he changed the subject to his blood pressure — and because the rep followed with a generic motivation monologue about men with children rather than tying accountability back to the specific evidence sitting in front of him, which was two weeks of unsupervised training that had just injured the man's back. Worth building a play for: this objection will recur with self-made business owners.

notes: Score this one as provisional — the transcript is truncated at 00:18:24 and Phases 5 through 11 are unobservable, so the phase weights that matter most for outcome are missing. On what is visible, this is the best-executed front half in the batch: the only genuine use of the application, and by a distance the most thorough baseline, including the two questions the rep skips everywhere else — occupation with a quantified sitting percentage, and injuries pursued past the first vague answer. Two coaching points are already visible. First, he consistently finds the emotional territory and then talks over it; when the prospect said 'I'm too fat to keep up with my daughters' the correct move was a question and a silence, and what followed was a monologue about how men with kids perform better, after which the prospect changed the subject. Second, he let the single strongest piece of evidence on the call go by: this man is currently self-coaching from Trevor's free videos and has hurt his back doing it, which is Phase 4's 'why can't you stick to it on your own' answering itself, and the rep replied 'It's good to start.' Above the coaching: the clinical picture here — diagnosed disc compression, a subluxing knee, a locked hip, hypertension at 105 kg, and a fresh training injury — needs a clearance question that the playbook does not contain, and re-pulling the full recording should be treated as a prerequisite to any decision about this prospect.
